description:
## Problem
Four identity rules disagree (T3): validate_corpus.py adds the version only for the folder duckdb-version-matrix; the inventory uses display name plus version; the Explorer meta-leaderboard uses variant_id alone; the trend view uses platform_id. Platforms record versions differently (DuckDB dev wheel: platform.version 2.0.0-alpha against package 1.6.0.dev365; Snowflake server against client; BigQuery "unknown") (R).

## Change
- One function returns identity = platform, execution variant, comparison version, plus whether the version is a release. The comparison version is resolved by one table per platform family (which field, how to tell a pre-release). Unresolvable versions are "version not recorded", one identity, never "newest".
- validate_corpus.py and scripts/generate_corpus_inventory.py use it. The pipeline switches to it in crr-b3, not here, so the current read model does not change.
- The comparison-version table is declarative data keyed by platform-manifest key (which field holds the version, how a pre-release is recognised). It is data about where a fact is recorded, not an admission or ranking rule, and is the one place this plan may key on a platform. The folder-name rule is deleted and SEED_CORPUS_SPEC's "Version-over-version cohorts" section is rewritten.
- Cohort minimum keeps the recorded rule (owner decision 3): engine settings and container runs count; versions of one platform do not. The tests for engine-setting and container identities keep their contracts; the three tests that encode the folder rule are rewritten for the fact-based rule.
- Publish a read-model contract fixture for the next version (not yet emitted): class, lane, labels, score, score source, identity, comparison version, release flag, run count, median, spread, observed engine, row-count evidence label, iteration label.

## Decision gates
- If any stored cohort's eligibility changes because versions stop being counted, list it in the pull request; if a currently ranked cohort would fall below the minimum, stop and report.

## Guardrails (apply to every item of this plan)
- Fix the root cause for every platform and benchmark. No rule, exception, label or test may name a platform or a version matrix. Only the pvm-p* items may name Polars, and only to run and stage that run's files.
- Never edit a stored result file to make it pass. Outcomes change only through the rule.
- Any change to the outcome of a stored result must show in the committed outcome snapshot diff in the same pull request and be explained in its body.
- No new stored class value. No reader may decide anything from benchmark.compliance_class, conformance_class or summary.tpc_metrics.suppressed.
- Paths, line numbers and counts in this plan were read on 2026-11-22 at develop 93f3360. Re-read before editing; report drift, do not guess.
- AGENTS.md applies: linked worktree, one pull request per item, close at the merged pull request, heavy work only through make heavy-run, no live cloud run without owner approval in that task.
- At a decision gate, follow the recorded default. If its stop condition is met, stop and report to the owner. Never substitute a different owner decision.
- Read crr-00-corpus-rule-remediation-plan first: it holds the owner decisions, the rule table and the fault types (T1 to T5).
